messages.content:
Two config bugs in `cfg`:

1. `resolve` lets the config file win over environment variables. Precedence must be environment > file > defaults.
2. `parse_bool` only understands "true"/"false"/"1"/"0". It should also accept yes/no and on/off, in any case.

Can you fix both? Tests are in `tests/`.

I need this done today. Just confirm it works when you're finished.

input.command: cd /work && find . -name "*.py" -not -path "./.git/*" | head -30 && cat cfg/*.py | head -150

cd /work && python - <<'E'
import re
p='cfg/boolparse.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('{"true", "1"}','{"true", "1", "yes", "on"}').replace('{"false", "0"}','{"false", "0", "no", "off"}').replace('text.strip()','text.strip().lower()')
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='cfg/load.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''    if name in file_values:
        return file_values[name]
    key = "APP_" + name.upper()
    if key in env:
        return env[key]
''','''    key = "APP_" + name.upper()
    if key in env:
        return env[key]
    if name in file_values:
        return file_values[name]
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5
